content.description: The greenhouse effect is not a problem in itself: it is the invisible blanket that keeps the Earth from freezing. The real trouble starts when we thicken it too fast.

hero.hook: Without the greenhouse effect, the Earth would be a desert of ice. With too much of it, the planet overheats.

blocks.text: Picture a closed car in the sun: the windows let the light in, but the heat struggles to get back out. The inside warms up. The Earth's [[greenhouse effect]] works a little like that, with air in place of glass.

The phenomenon is **natural** and vital. Without it, the average temperature of the globe would drop toward **-18°C**. With it, we sit around **+15°C**. Today's problem is not that it exists: it is the rapid **amplification** caused by our own activities.
The Sun mainly sends visible light. The atmosphere lets it through. The ground and the oceans warm up, then send that energy back as **infrared heat**, waves “longer” than visible light.

blocks.caption: Industrial emissions strengthen the greenhouse effect

blocks.text: Certain gases, the [[greenhouse gases]], absorb that heat and send it back in every direction, including down toward the ground. Nitrogen and oxygen, which make up most of the air, barely do this job at all. Water vapor, **CO₂** and **methane** do it very well.
The name “greenhouse effect” is a little misleading. A real greenhouse warms up mainly by blocking the hot air that rises. The atmosphere traps heat in another way, by absorbing infrared rays.

sections.title: How the planet keeps its heat

blocks.text: Since the industrial revolution, we have burned coal, oil and gas. That carbon, buried underground for millions of years, goes straight back into the air. Deforestation also removes the forests that used to absorb CO₂. Livestock and rice growing add methane, about **80 times** more warming than CO₂ over 20 years.

The result: the concentration of CO₂ has gone from about **280** to more than **420** parts per million. Such a level had not been seen since the [[Pliocene]], roughly **3 million years** ago, when the seas stood higher.
The [[IPCC]], which pulls together the work of thousands of climate scientists, is blunt: the warming since 1950 has no precedent over thousands of years, and its human origin is established.

More energy in the air and the oceans means sharper extremes: drier droughts, more violent rain, melting glaciers and ice caps, rising seas. And there is an accelerator: when the white ice vanishes, dark ground and dark water soak up more sunlight. That is [[terrestrial albedo]] falling, and the planet warms faster still.
Venus shows the greenhouse effect “running away”: an atmosphere that is 96% CO₂, and about **460°C** at ground level, hot enough to melt lead.

sections.title: What a more energetic climate changes

blocks.text: The international goal is to stay under **+1.5°C** or **+2°C** compared with the pre-industrial era, to avoid dangerous thresholds such as the thawing of the [[permafrost]], which would release even more methane.
Two levers: **cut** emissions (clean energy, using less, forests) and **adapt** to what is already locked in. CO₂ stays in the air for centuries, so what we emit today weighs on us for a long time.
Without the natural greenhouse effect, the Earth would freeze toward **-18°C**. Amplifying it with fossil fuels has pushed CO₂ to levels not seen for **3 million years**.

sections.title: Limit the rise, adapt to the rest

content.title: What is the greenhouse effect (really)?

GHG.explanation: Gases that absorb infrared radiation emitted by the Earth and re-emit it, warming the atmosphere. The main ones are: water vapor (natural), CO₂, methane (CH₄, 80x more powerful than CO₂ over 20 years), and N₂O.

Greenhouse gases.explanation: Gases that absorb infrared radiation emitted by the Earth and re-emit it, warming the atmosphere. The main ones are: water vapor (natural), CO₂, methane (CH₄, 80x more powerful than CO₂ over 20 years), and N₂O.

Greenhouse gases (GHG).explanation: Gases that absorb infrared radiation emitted by the Earth and re-emit it, warming the atmosphere. The main ones are: water vapor (natural), CO₂, methane (CH₄, 80x more powerful than CO₂ over 20 years), and N₂O.

IPCC.explanation: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, created in 1988 to assess scientific information related to climate change.

Pliocene.explanation: Geological epoch spanning from approximately 5.3 to 2.5 million years before the present, often used as a comparison point for current CO2 levels.

Terrestrial albedo.explanation: The ability of a surface to reflect solar radiation. Ice and snow have a high albedo (reflect a lot), oceans have a low albedo (absorb more). Melting ice reduces the global albedo, accelerating warming.

greenhouse effect.explanation: Natural warming process of a planet by its atmosphere, where certain gases adsorb and re-emit thermal radiation from the surface.

greenhouse gases.explanation: Gases that absorb infrared radiation emitted by the Earth and re-emit it, warming the atmosphere. The main ones are: water vapor (natural), CO₂, methane (CH₄, 80x more powerful than CO₂ over 20 years), and N₂O.

permafrost.explanation: Part of a soil permanently frozen for at least two consecutive years, storing huge amounts of organic carbon.

terrestrial albedo.explanation: The ability of a surface to reflect solar radiation. Ice and snow have a high albedo (reflect a lot), oceans have a low albedo (absorb more). Melting ice reduces the global albedo, accelerating warming.

quiz.explanation: The ground heated by the Sun radiates infrared heat; certain gases absorb it and return it in all directions, including towards the ground.
options: Gases absorb infrared heat returned from the ground and send it back to itself
The Sun directly sends more heat on certain days
The atmosphere blocks visible light from the Sun
The ground produces its own heat independently of the Sun
quiz.question: What is actually happening to cause the greenhouse effect to warm the Earth?

quiz.explanation: Without a natural greenhouse effect, the average global temperature would drop to around -18°C, compared to around +15°C today.
quiz.question: Without the greenhouse effect, to what average temperature would the globe fall?

quiz.explanation: Nitrogen and oxygen hardly do this job: it is mainly water vapor, CO2 and methane that absorb infrared heat.
options: True
False
quiz.question: True or false: nitrogen and oxygen, present in the majority in the air, play a major role in the greenhouse effect.

quiz.explanation: Since the industrial revolution, the combustion of coal, oil and gas has released carbon into the air that has remained buried for millions of years.
options: CO2 from the combustion of coal, oil and gas
Nitrogen released by agriculture
Ozone produced by cars
Helium from weather balloons
quiz.question: Which gas mainly explains the increase in the greenhouse effect since the industrial revolution?

quiz.explanation: Raising and growing rice adds methane, about 80 times hotter than CO2 over a 20-year period.
quiz.question: Approximately how many times more does methane heat up than CO2 over 20 years?

quiz.explanation: The concentration of CO2 increased from about 280 to more than 420 parts per million, a level not seen in about 3 million years.
quiz.question: How many parts per million (ppm) has the concentration of CO2 in the air risen today, compared to 280 ppm before the industrial era?

quiz.explanation: The IPCC synthesizes the work of thousands of climatologists and concludes that the warming since 1950 is unprecedented and of human origin.
options: The group that synthesizes the work of thousands of climatologists
An international oil company
An international treaty on biodiversity
A space agency that monitors the climate
quiz.question: What is the IPCC, mentioned in the course?

quiz.explanation: When the white ice disappears, the dark soil and water absorb more sunlight: this is the decline in the Earth's albedo, which further accelerates warming.
options: Dark soil and water, revealed, absorb more sunlight than white ice
Melted ice directly releases CO2
Melt water first cools the atmosphere and then heats it more
Glaciers emit methane as they melt
quiz.question: Why does melting ice further accelerate warming?

quiz.explanation: On Venus, an atmosphere of 96% CO2 brings the ground temperature to around 460°C, enough to melt lead.
options: True
False
quiz.question: True or false: On Venus, the ground is hot enough to melt lead.
